replacements.old:
The all-rate estimand prevents the argument from collapsing onto one fortunate learning rate, while
five checkpoint stages reveal whether an advantage emerges early, accumulates gradually, or
disappears. The result remains specific to the tested DenseOn adaptation problem; it is stronger
than a best-cell comparison and weaker than a universal optimizer ranking.
replacements.new:
The all-rate comparison estimates performance averaged over the specified grids; validation-based
selection estimates the outcome of choosing a recipe within those grids. These answer different
questions, and neither defines a universal optimizer ranking. Five checkpoint stages additionally
show when retrieval differences emerge and whether they persist. All conclusions remain specific
to this DenseOn adaptation problem and the tested learning-rate ranges.
